item.title: Sacred Heart Academy claims SCC volleyball title over Amity behind JJ Kirck's 31 digs
item.description: The Sacred Heart Academy girls volleyball team celebrates its SCC title after beating Amity 3-2 on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, at West Haven High School. (Mike Madera/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HAVEN - It is often said that offense wins games and defense wins championships. Sacred Heart Academy senior libero JJ Kirck will attest to that. Playing spectacular defense, including 31 digs, Kirck was one of the keys in leading the second-seeded Sharks to a 3-2 (21-25, 25-11, 25-19, 23-25, 15-11) victory over top-seeded Amity in the Southern Connecticut Conference championship game at West Haven High on Thursday evening. "Our team battled all year," Kirck said after being named the tournament's Most Outstanding Player. "We played so many different games this year, and every game besides one, we came out on top. Tonight was just a show of how much we faced adversity." The Sharks avenged consecutive SCC championship game losses to Amity and improved to 20-1 on the season. "It means everything to me," Kirck said. "I'm from Amity. I love all these girls across the net. I grew up playing volleyball with all of them. I am so glad my senior year, I was able to get the dub, and I am so glad I was able to do it with my best friends." Both teams entered the contest without losing a set thus far in the SCC tournament. Amity, which has been in the final every year since 2021 and won two in a row over the Sharks, delivered the first blow in handing Sacred Heart Academy its first set loss of the tournament by riding the play of Calleigh Parkin and Brooke Cichon in the opening set. The Sharks pushed back and dominated the second set with a 14-point win that saw a kill by Aliya Church put the Sharks ahead 16-8 and her ace extend the lead to 20-9. "Their defense played really well," Amity coach Seth Davis said after his team fell to 19-3 on the year. "They dig a lot of balls. They pass really well. Once we started passing, we could keep the ball in system and get the ball to Olive (Hubbard)." The two teams used strong defensive play to split the next two sets as Kirck's defense thwarted Amity in the third set before she closed it out with a pair of service points. The Spartans would not go quietly, overcoming a 21-19 fourth-set deficit with a pair of kills by SCC Player of the Year Olive Hubbard, a kill by Parkin, and a block by Hubbard to close the set. "We did our job from the service line," Sacred Heart Academy coach Dave Alexandro said. "Tough serves to the seams, and it kind of took them out of system which allowed us to get some swings on the ball, and then build up a little bit of a lead. With that confidence, swinging well, hitting the ball well, kind of moving them around the court made a big difference." The turning point came in the fifth set when a block by Paige Nelson gave Sacred Heart Academy a 10-9 lead. item.title: Elder's Kaden Estep is rewriting Panther records in senior season
item.description: Nearly 40 years ago, Steve Keller dominated the Elder Panther quarterback records. The starting quarterback in 1987 and 1988, Keller amassed 4,816 yards and 45 touchdowns in his career. Twenty years after Keller, Mark Miller led Elder to the Division I state championship game in 2008 and the semifinals in 2009. Along the way, he broke both of Keller's career records with 5,872 yards and 56 touchdowns. Miller's touchdown record still stands, but his yardage record didn't get that 20-year cushion. First, Peyton Ramsey broke it with 6,708 yards (and took second with 49 touchdowns) from 2013 to 2015, but the Elder record books were rewritten again in 2026 and the pencil is still sharpened to take down another. Elder senior quarterback and Cincinnati Bearcats commit Kaden Estep broke Ramsey's record with a 13-yard pass to Jake Bier in a 62-6 win over Mount Zion Prep on Oct. 23. Estep finished the game with 6,861 career passing yards. His five touchdown passes in that game put him at 53 for his career, just three behind Miller. "Earned," Ramsey, now an assistant coach at Elder, posted on X after Estep's record-breaking night . "The greatest QB to ever put on the uniform. Period. An absolute winner. All of it a byproduct of the type of teammate he is. Keep going!" Since Estep took over as a sophomore in 2024, Elder has gone 26-9, including an undefeated 2025 regular season and Greater Catholic-League South championship . It was Elder's first GCL-South crown since Ramsey led Elder to a split with St. Xavier in 2015 and first solo title since Miller led the Panthers in '08. Name Years Passing yards Touchdowns Kaden Estep 2023-26 6,861 53 Peyton Ramsey 2013-15 6,708 49 Mark Miller 2008-09 5,872 56 Steve Keller 1987-88 4,816 45 Miller, now a teacher at Taylor, was previously the head coach for the Yellowjackets after coaching junior varsity at Elder. Seeing Ramsey initially break his yardage record was a full-circle moment. "I remember Peyton and I remember one of (assistant coach) Craig James' sons, Jakob, being ball boys and running around," Miller said. "Your typical coach's kid that Peyton is has been living, breathing and eating Elder football since the time he could walk, I'm sure. "It's been fun to watch to kind of watch him progress from the player that I got to watch after I graduated to the coach and the teacher that he is now." Miller got an early look at what Coach Peyton Ramsey would look like when Ramsey was just starting his college career at Indiana. "I texted him," Miller said. "I was like, 'Hey, I need your help on drawing some of these plays up because I've been removed far enough now where all this language is new.' When I asked (Elder head coach) Doug (Ramsey), I said, 'Doug, do you have a playbook for me?' And I'll never forget it; he literally pointed to his head and that was it. I was like, 'Well, I'm going to need some help from the guy who was just here.' "Even then and obviously as a player, he was special and could break things d

item.title: 2027: Ekiti PDP, SDP, APM, others unite for Tinubu
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela & Omeiza Ajayi ADO-EKITI — President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign received a boost in Ekiti State yesterday, as governorship candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Social Democratic Party. SDP, and Allied Peoples Movement, APM, declared support for his second-term bid. The opposition politicians made their declarations at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where Governor Biodun Oyebanji pledged that the state would deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, the President urged Ekiti residents to improve on the 201,495 votes secured by the APC in the state in the 2023 presidential election, when the party won in all 16 local government areas. Dignitaries at the rally included; Ondo State Governor, Dr Lucky Aiyedatiwa; Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele; and former Ekiti governors, Ayodele Fayose, Kayode Fayemi and Niyi Adebayo. Shettima said the support of opposition candidates and former governors demonstrated the growing political strength of the APC in the state. He also recalled that Oyebanji secured 85.74 per cent of the votes in the June governorship election, expressing optimism that the party could garner between 90 and 95 per cent in the presidential poll. “With a total registered vote of 1,028,000, it is our hope, prayer and aspiration that from January 16, 2027, APC will garner 90 to 95 per cent of the votes cast in Ekiti State,” Shettima said. Oyebanji promises 90% Oyebanji described the rally as a demonstration of political unity, saying the support of former opposition candidates and former governors had strengthened the APC ahead of the presidential election. He recalled that Tinubu, during his 2022 campaign, had urged Ekiti residents to vote for both him and Oyebanji, promising federal support for the state if elected. According to the governor, the President has fulfilled that promise through what he described as unprecedented federal interventions in Ekiti since its creation 30 years ago. Oyebanji pledged that the state would improve on its previous electoral performance and deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for the President. APC targets 800,000 votes Also speaking, Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, challenged Ekiti to deliver 800,000 votes for Tinubu, representing about 90 per cent of the votes expected from the state. He said: “Out of 1,080,000 votes, and PVC collected over 900,000, this is my request, and by extension, of course, of the President to you. We are looking for 800,000 votes, representing about 90 per cent.” North firmly behind Tinubu — YARI “We in Northern Nigeria, Bola is more of us than you in Ekiti, than you in Ondo, than you in Oyo, than you in Osun, than you in Lagos. item.title: Why Grizzlies’ Isaiah Stewart has ‘no regrets’ on wild LeBron James altercation
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Why Grizzlies’ Isaiah Stewart has ‘no regrets’ on wild LeBron James altercation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Isaiah Stewart has built a reputation as one of the NBA’s most fiery players, and the Memphis Grizzlies big man is not about to apologize for it. Looking back on his infamous altercation with LeBron James and other run-ins, Stewart made it clear he does not regret a thing. In an interview with Andscape, Stewart was asked whether he had any regrets about those incidents or if it was simply the emotion of the moment. “I don’t have no regrets. You know, I feel like there’s lessons out of everything. You know, even going back to that first incident, you know, Charlotte, like I don’t have no regrets and I don’t care what people may perceive me as,” Stewart said. “I come to play basketball and I play the game a certain way. And it has been times where, you know, I thought back and say, hey, I shouldn’t have done that.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Isaiah Stewart says he has no regrets about trying to fight LeBron James 😳 (Via @andscape / h/t @0xBassey ) pic.twitter.com/WrXxsGevz9 — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 5, 2026 Stewart also called out opponents he believes try to bait him into losing his cool. “And I feel like teams having their game plan of, hey, let’s do something to trip him off, to get him out the game. For me, it’s hard to respect you as a man if that’s your game plan,” he said. The LeBron incident remains the most memorable of Stewart’s career. Back in November 2021, James struck Stewart in the face with an elbow while the two were battling for position during a free throw, leaving the then-Detroit Pistons big man bloodied. An enraged Stewart repeatedly charged after James and had to be held back. James was ejected and later suspended one game, while Stewart received a two-game suspension. His most recent suspension came in February 2026, when Stewart left the bench to join a fight between the Pistons and the Charlotte Hornets . The NBA handed him a seven-game ban, citing his “repeated history of unsportsmanlike acts.” It was his fourth suspension for fighting. A few months later, Detroit traded Stewart to the Grizzlies for three future second-round picks during the 2026 NBA Draf t, ending his six-season run with the Pistons. Now 25 years old, Stewart is part of a Grizzlies team that is off to a 6-2 start. Based on his comments, he has no plans of changing the way he plays anytime soon. item.title: Unfair NIL: Millionaire Quarterbacks, Broke Linemen
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Auburn Tigers offensive lineman Jacobe' Ward (74) blocks during the third quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The numbers are finally in, and they tell a story that leaves many fans scratching their heads. A new database released on Friday by the College Sports Commission reveals just how wide the gap is between star quarterbacks and the players in the trenches. According to Fox Sports , the market is bearing a heavy load for some while others fly blind. John Bramlette, the head of operations for the commission, admitted that “Everyone to some degree or another has probably been flying blind as far as what the market is actually bearing.” This lack of clarity has left schools and athletes guessing for far too long. The Millionaire Quarterback vs. The Working Class Lineman Let’s be honest about the disparity. The data shows that the top 10 percent of paid Power Four quarterbacks are receiving $1.611 million in revenue share alone, with combined NIL and revenue-share totals climbing higher at the extreme end. That official College Sports Commission figure lines up with earlier summer estimates from Opendorse and others that already put elite quarterbacks well into seven figures. Meanwhile, the median pay for players in other spots, like the offensive line or defensive back, is a fraction of that. It is a system where the face of the program gets the big checks , but the guys blocking for him are often just scraping by. This is about football and who gets valued in the eyes of the market. The report sorted the money by position and conference, giving us a clear look at the divide. The revenue sharing for the top tier hit $662,000, making the gap between Power Four and non-Power Four schools in men’s basketball dramatic regarding high-end spending. Football follows a similar pattern, but the stakes for the players at the bottom are much higher. The data might not capture every single dollar, but it reflects the reality that many players have tried to report on in less official ways.

item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Oregon came in at No. 23 in the initial rankings, revealed live on ESPN on Tuesday. Dan Lanning’s team is on the outside looking in at the 12-team playoff, one season before a 24-team playoff is set to likely go into effect. The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll. But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC. Other Big Ten teams in this week’s CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana. item.title: Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? Making sense of trade rumors around star RB
item.description: Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? Making sense of trade rumors around star RB originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Ravens , once 4-1 and near the top of the AFC, are in serious trouble after four consecutive losses. Not only is Baltimore last in the AFC North at 4-5, but the Ravens might not have Lamar Jackson back on the field this season after thumb surgery. Help is on the way, as veteran Jacoby Brissett is coming over from the Cardinals in a trade to take over at quarterback, but it might take a heroic effort for Baltimore to turn its season around. With the trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, would the Ravens consider trading future Hall of Fame RB Derrick Henry? Here's what you need to know about the rumors surrounding Henry. MORE: Can Ravens still make the playoffs? Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? The future of Henry is something to "keep half an eye on," ESPN's Dan Graziano reported before the Ravens' loss to the Jaguars . "Henry is turning 33 in January. He is scheduled to earn $12 million next year, and none of that money is guaranteed," Graziano said. "If he isn't in Baltimore's plans beyond this year, the Ravens could find themselves fielding offers over the next week." Fielding offers isn't the same as shopping a player, but as the math becomes more difficult for the Ravens in the AFC, Graziano lists a handful of reasons why a trade could make sense, from Henry's age and contract to the reality of trying to win without Jackson. The number of contenders in need of a running back could also get the Ravens some value in a trade. Several teams, including the Giants , Broncos , Bengals , Vikings and Packers , have been reported as suitors for Indianapolis' Jonathan Taylor. Only one of them can get him. Could the losers of that sweepstakes make a play for Henry? Teams being interested in Henry is no surprise. The Ravens willingly talking about deals involving Henry is a separate subject, and to this point, no reports have indicated they are looking to deal their running back. With Brissett coming in and a more favorable portion of the schedule ahead, one would think Baltimore still has visions of competing this season. If the Ravens wanted to get something for Henry, though, the best time might be right now. item.title: Ravens’ TNF nightmare gets even worse with concerning Kyle Hamilton injury
item.description: Mitch Stringer-Imagn Images Ravens’ TNF nightmare gets even worse with concerning Kyle Hamilton injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens just can’t catch a break with all the injuries . Already down to their third-string quarterback, the Ravens have now lost safety Kyle Hamilton for the rest of their Thursday Night Football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Hamilton will not return after suffering a hip injury . He had already been dealing with a knee injury that kept him out of practice the previous week . The Ravens look on course to lose their fourth game in a row. As of this writing, they are down 33-10 to the Jaguars in the fourth quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) A first-round pick by the Ravens in 2022, Hamilton came into Thursday night as the team’s second-leading tackler behind Roquan Smith with 57 tackles in eight games. He also has one interception and a forced fumble. Hamilton’s injury adds to the Ravens’ already lengthy injury list in the secondary. Cornerback Nate Wiggins was listed as inactive shortly before the Jags game due to illness . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins was also listed as out. It remains to be seen whether this latest injury will keep Hamilton out for their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers. But they will have a lengthy 11-day break before that game, which should give him time to recover. But if it is in any way serious, the Ravens are unlikely to risk sending him out amid his other injury concerns. With the Ravens’ season increasingly looking lost amid their quarterback injuries, they will be wise to exercise caution moving forward. item.title: Terrorists abduct 10 in Ogun, demand 25m ransom
item.description: By Adeola Badru Families of 10 travellers, including a former member of the National Youth Service Corps NYSC, Olusoji Adedapo, have raised the alarm over their abduction at Ijebu Awa, a boundary community between Ogun and Oyo states, with the kidnappers demanding N25 million for their release. Although unconfirmed reports indicated that some of the passengers were serving corps members, the police said none of those abducted was a corps member. The 24-year-old Adedapo, reportedly completed his national service in Edo State last week and was travelling to Ibadan when the incident occurred on Tuesday. His cousin, Adeseye Timilehin, who disclosed this, said the family had been thrown into distress, particularly as the kidnappers had issued a 24-hour deadline for payment of the ransom. He explained that Dapo (Adedapo) had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication. Timilehin said the family learnt of the abduction shortly after 7pm on Tuesday, when one of the passengers reportedly escaped and contacted another family member. He explained that Dapo was travelling with a friend, Tunde, with whom he had served during the NYSC programme, informing that Tunde was the only passenger who managed to escape the attack and alerted the family. According to him: “On Tuesday morning, my cousin left Benin City, Edo State. He was posted to Edo State for NYSC and did his Passing-Out Ceremony last week. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan. “He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic in Benin. I have the videos of the traffic jam on my phone. By the time they were able to get out of the traffic, it was already 3pm. “They kept telling the driver that it was already late and that they should return to Benin and continue the journey the following day, but the driver insisted on going. By the time they got to Ijebu at about 7pm, they were attacked by the bandits.” He noted d that Tunde told him the driver had swerved into the bush and stopped immediately after the gunmen appeared in front of the vehicle, forcing the passengers to flee for safety. “He told me that when the driver swerved into the bush and stopped, the bandits immediately jumped in front of their bus. He had to hide in the bush while the rest ran for safety and were captured. He was able to escape, but my brother and the others were taken away,” he said. Timilehin said the family subsequently established contact with Tunde, who provided further details of the incident and confirmed that police officers had arrived at the scene, rescued him and taken him to a police station, where he spent the night. He said the survivor also informed the family that a search party had been deployed into the surrounding forest that same night to locate the abducted passengers, but the operation did not yield any positive result. item.title: ‘He’s special’: Ayo Dosunmu says Timberwolves have a ‘trash talker’ who’s just like Muhammad Ali
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Ayo Dosunmu has heaped praise on Anthony Edwards and has compared the Minnesota Timberwolves star to Muhammad Ali and three NBA greats. The 26-year-old joined the Wolves in February this year, and he has built a great relationship with all of his new teammates in Minnesota. Edwards, in particular, has become a good pal, and Dosunmu has given an insight into what the Ant-Man is actually like. Ayo Dosunmu compares Anthony Edwards to Muhammad Ali Edwards is arguably the biggest star on the Minnesota Timberwolves roster. The 25-year-old had an unbelievable start to the season, but is currently sidelined following surgery on his knee. The initial diagnosis was that he would be out for around two months. The Timberwolves have missed Edwards, but everyone associated with the team is convinced that he will come back stronger. That is because of his mentality, which every member of the Wolves roster has constantly seen – not just during games but in practice as well. Dosunmu said about Edwards in The Players’ Tribune : “Ant. He’s special. As a trash talker, he’s like what you hear about with the Kobe (Bryant) stories, the MJ (Michael Jordan) stories, the KG (Kevin Garnett) stories. No, really, I think a better comparison is like the (Muhammad) Ali stories. “He’s jogging back after a bucket like: ‘Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee! I’m a bad man! I’m so pretty!!!'” Edwards isn’t just a really talented player, but his personality is incredible as well. That is why he is so loved, not just by the fans but by his teammates as well. The Minnesota Timberwolves need their star man back. If he hits the ground running once he returns, there is every chance they will achieve their ambitions this season. item.title: Gabriel Vs. Magomedov: 4 Keys To Victory In ONE Lightweight MMA Main Event At ONE Fight Night 49
item.description: Two unbeaten runs collide in the main event of ONE Fight Night 49 on Prime Video , and only one will make it out intact. Lucas Gabriel puts his unblemished promotional record on the line against undefeated newcomer Magomed “Muhammad” Magomedov in a highly pivotal lightweight MMA showdown. The three-round war, carrying massive potential World Title implications, goes down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6. View this post on Instagram Gabriel has seamlessly carved through six appearances in ONE Championship without suffering a single defeat. The 26-year-old earned the most significant victory of his career this past June, outpointing former divisional king Ok Rae Yoon at ONE Fight Night 44 . With ONE Lightweight MMA World Champion Christian “The Warrior” Lee defending his crown against ONE Welterweight Submission Grappling World Champion Tye Ruotolo at The Inner Circle 37 , a statement win could instantly make Gabriel the undisputed next man in line. Magomedov, meanwhile, carries a flawless 15-0 professional record into his promotional debut. The KHK Dagestan standout fearlessly stepped in on short notice for the injured Alibeg Rasulov , making the leap to the global stage riding five consecutive finishes. With a high-level black belt’s craft set directly against suffocating Dagestani-style pressure, here are the four tactical keys that will ultimately decide which unbeaten run lives on. #1 Gabriel’s Scramble-Ready Guard Photo Credit: ONE Championship Putting a Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt on his back can create more problems than it solves. For Gabriel, the bottom is a launch point rather than a resting place, and he has already built a blueprint against wrestling-heavy opponents like Magomedov. That counts for plenty, because the ONE debutant will inevitably look to drag this fight to the canvas. The late opponent change hardly upended the Phuket Fight Club representative’s plans. His camp, conveniently, was already built around stopping Rasulov’s takedown-first mentality. Gabriel has been here before. He has beaten every grinding Russian wrestler ONE has put in front of him, neutralizing Kurbanali “Big Show” Isabekov for a dominant decision and submitting Gadzhimurad “Tought” Amirzhanov with an arm-triangle choke. This past February, he outworked Dagestani standout Magomed Akaev at ONE Fight Night 40 . Moreover, the Brazilian holds the experience edge, bringing a level of big-stage poise that Magomedov has yet to build in ONE. If Magomedov takes him down expecting control, he may find himself fighting off a seasoned submission threat who has cracked this code before. #2 Magomedov’s Counter-Takedowns View this post on Instagram Magomedov rarely shoots blind. Instead, he turns an opponent’s offense into his entry, catching kicks and changing levels under looping punches to put fights on the mat. His opportunistic timing makes it work. item.title: The 3 main reasons behind the Magic's slow start to 2026-27 season
item.description: The 3 main reasons behind the Magic's slow start to 2026-27 season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sean Sweeney era in Orlando could be off to a better start. The Magic dropped their third straight game on Thursday night, a 117-104 defeat against the Phoenix Suns despite a 27-point performance from Wendell Carter Jr. The loss dropped Orlando to 2-6 so far this season. For a team with playoff expectations, the Magic have dug themselves an early hole to climb out of — the path to the playoffs will not be easy, particularly if a few areas of concern aren't addressed. Here's a look at the three main reasons for the Magic's slow start in 2026-27. Reasons behind the Magic's slow start Injuries To put it plainly: the Magic are a much better team when Paolo Banchero is on the floor. That's no knock on Orlando — most NBA teams struggle without their best player. But after a 35-point night in the season-opener, Banchero has been out with a sprained ankle. Without Banchero, the Magic haven't had a go-to scorer, especially with Franz Wagner (41.9% from the floor) struggling to shoot the ball early this season. Orlando hasn't had a 30-point scorer since Banchero's opener against Atlanta, and it took 28 Desmond Bane points to beat the Raptors last week. Banchero was given a four-to-six week timeline, meaning the Magic still likely have plenty of time without him. And that's all without mentioning Jalen Suggs' absence, leaving an all-around impact on both ends of the floor vacant. Orlando needs Wagner to be more efficient as a three-level scorer, and for Bane to take over offensively more often. Without Banchero and Suggs, there are critical voids not being filled. Turnovers Entering Thursday's game, the Magic were averaging the sixth-most turnovers per game in the NBA, in the same territory as teams like the Nets , Bulls , Kings , Pelicans and Jazz . That isn't a group of teams Orlando expected to be in conversations with this season. That was before another 25 turnovers against the Suns, who came into the game with just one win this season. Wagner turned the ball over six times — though he did have 15 assists — and Anthony Black had another five turnovers. Particularly with Banchero and Suggs absent, the margin for error is thinner. The Magic need Wagner to take care of the ball as the lead star right now, and Sweeney's first Orlando team needs to play a much cleaner brand of basketball if it's going to turn things around. item.title: Magic rumors: Will Orlando blow up roster at trade deadline?
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Magic rumors: Will Orlando blow up roster at trade deadline? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It has been a rough start to the 2026-27 season for the Orlando Magic despite being under the tutelage of new head coach Sean Sweeney, whom they hired from the San Antonio Spurs this past offseason. They entered their Thursday night clash against the Phoenix Suns with a 2-5 record, and considering their player payroll and injury situation, falling behind in the playoff race this early has to be ringing some alarm bells. The Magic have been ravaged by the injury bug; Paolo Banchero’s strong start to the campaign was abruptly cut by a high ankle sprain that will keep him out for four to six weeks, and Jalen Suggs followed him on the injured list shortly after suffering a non-contact knee injury. If the Magic keep on losing and fall way off the pace, there are some difficult decisions for their front office to make, as ClutchPoints insider Tomer Azarly noted on the latest episode of the Clutch Scoops show. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “They have some difficult decisions on their hand. I think Orlando has a good roster, I just don’t know if they’re good enough to make any legitimate noise in the Eastern Conference. I think I’m gonna buy that they miss the playoffs,” Azarly said. Latest trade rumors/intel: Warriors, Thunder | Clutch Scoops with @TomerAzarly & @BrettSiegelNBA https://t.co/vjgWFuHgEd — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 5, 2026 ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel then seconded this motion, and he even took it a step further by saying that the Magic will become a selling team at the trade deadline. “I also buy the fact that the Magic are going to become sellers at the trade deadline. This core just has not worked out. This is a group of what could have been. Injuries have just been a major setback for them,” Siegel added. The Magic have an expensive core (they already have around $174 million committed to their core four of Banchero, Franz Wagner, Suggs, and Wendell Carter Jr.), and they will need to re-sign Anthony Black to a new deal with the 22-year-old set to enter restricted free agency at the end of this campaign. If they miss the postseason entirely, there could indeed be some roster reshuffling in Orlando.

item.title: Jaguars Defense Drowns Ravens in Rainy Baltimore
item.description: Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile looks on before an NFL football matchup at EverBank Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. The Jaguars defeated the Browns 34-10. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jacksonville Jaguars weathered the storm in Baltimore, and the Ravens had no answer for the elements or Anthony Campanile’s defense. In a rainy Thursday night showdown, Jacksonville completely smothered Baltimore, turning a hostile road environment into a blowout victory. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 9 33-10 road win over the Baltimore Ravens. Favorite Highlight: Mr. Consensus Boards, tight end Nate Boerkircher, adjusting on the fly to Trevor Lawrence’s extended scramble, was exactly what Jacksonville needed to get the game started early. Boerkircher with a great adjustment for 52 yards, pic.twitter.com/ICvAg2otKI — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) November 6, 2026 Post-game notables: Taking The Show on the Road After three home blowout victories in the 2026 season, the Jacksonville Jaguars put together their first multi-score victory away from Duval County. A looming question heading into this matchup was whether Liam Coen’s squad could replicate their clear home dominance (+85-point win differential) when on the road. On Thursday, they answered this call, and then some. Turnover Party Anthony Campanile’s defense dominated rookie undrafted free agent quarterback Joe Fagnano in a clear way, limiting the Baltimore quarterback to 60 total passing yards, sacking him once, forcing two interceptions, and allowing no touchdowns (a 22.7 passer rating). Notably, a passer rating for simply hiking and spiking the ball earns a 39.6. To put this performance in context: Baltimore wide receiver Zay Flowers caught just one more Fagnano pass attempt than the Jacksonville defense. Additionally, Jacksonville has allowed just 10 first-quarter points this season, fewest in the NFL. Liam Coen’s Continued Dominance As noted by Jaguars on SI’s John Shipley, since 2024, Liam Coen offenses have averaged 36 points per game when facing defenses run by Jesse Minter. The 2024 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with Coen as the offensive coordinator, scored 40 points; Jacksonville scored 35 against the Chargers in Week 11 of 2025; the team scored 33 on Thursday. Tight Ends Matter The Jacksonville tight end room combined for 6 catches for 98 yards on Sunday, in a dominant showing of offensive versatility. item.title: Three takeaways from Michigan State's win over Toledo
item.description: Michigan State basketball improved to 2-0 on the season Thursday night when the Spartans defeated the Toledo Rockets, 91-61. It was another convincing win from MSU, who are showing the strength of this team early in the year. In the win, Michigan State had four in double figures, while the team shot 50.9% from the field to go along with a stellar 41.7% three-point percentage. The team outrebounded the Rockets 52-27, but lost the turnover battle 14-11. In the end, the Spartans got a convincing win over the Rockets, and continued to show that the hype that came into the season was warranted. Take a look at the three takeaways Spartans Wire had from the win over Toledo: 1. Another convincing win It may be a 37-point win over Quinnipiac and a 30-point win over Toledo, but the Spartans taking care of inferior competition and doing it in convincing fashion should not go unnoticed. Too many teams of the past, or other top ranked teams find themselves letting lesser teams hang around, but the Spartans taking care of their business shows a lot about this team. Being able to come in and dominate games like this shows that this team is ready to be a big time player across the landscape of college basketball this season. 2. Jasiah Jervis In the win against Toledo, it was Jasiah Jervis's coming out party. The true freshman finished with 16-points on 5-of-9 shooting, while going 4-for-7 from three. After a underwhelming debut against the Bobcats, it was great to see Jervis excel against Toledo. If the Spartans are going to hit their ceiling this season, Jervis is going to have to be a major component in the Spartans success. 3. Free throw shooting After two good things, there has to come a bad, and that is the Spartans free throw shooting. After a 15-for-26 night against Quinnipiac from the line, the Spartans followed it up with a 23-for-38 performance agaisnt the Rockets. There is no secret here, this is pitiful and Tom Izzo knows it. The Spartans are going to need to drastically improve their performance at the line if the team plans to have success in the tough road ahead. item.title: Brandon Aiyuk owes 49ers $13M as NFL return comes with complications
item.description: Brandon Aiyuk’s return to the NFL comes with several complications. The estranged 49ers wide receiver is set to return to the team facility Friday afternoon, but the reunion is sure to be awkward. The latest report states Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture , according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. The 49ers paid Brandon Aiyuk a $23 million signing bonus in 2024 and a $22.9 million option bonus in 2025, which totals $45.9 million. Aiyuk officially left the team about three-fourths of the way through the 2025 season, thus a 28% bonus forfeiture is owed. Brandon Aiyuk reportedly owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture. Getty Images The NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are attempting to resolve the situation. The sides could reach an agreement to pay back the money or it could go to arbitration. Regardless, the situation is complicated and may take time to find a solution. This muddles Aiyuk’s push to play football again, and Pelissero notes that the money is a “a potential complication in his efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday.” San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan. AP Photo/Kelley L. Cox 49ers general manager John Lynch. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 49ers have not unveiled their plans in the Aiyuk saga, but could allow him to join the team, release or trade him. Additionally, the 28-year-old has an outstanding warrant for his arrest in Santa Clara, further complicating the entire situation. Head coach Kyle Shanahan didn’t completely shut the door on an Aiyuk reunion , saying: “There’s no absolutes in life, so.” But the severed relationship certainly comes at a cost for both sides. Aiyuk and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, will report to the 49ers’ facility at 3 p.m. Friday, which should propel the next chapter into the ongoing saga between the receiver and the team. item.title: High School Coach Refuses to Apologize For Winning
item.description: Westlake head coach Rick Clausen directs his players during a practice on Aug. 11, 2026, at Westlake High. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Rick Clausen is not backing down from the parents who hired private investigators to dig into his Westlake High School program. The coach told the California Post on Thursday that he has zero intention of saying sorry for fixing a team that went 0-10 in 2024. He called the letter from “Concerned Westlake High School Parents” comical and stated that nothing shocks him in today’s society. This is a clear line in the sand for a coach who turned a floundering squad into a 7-3 playoff team in just two years. The parents sent a five-paragraph letter to the school on October 28. They claimed they were under the direction of legal counsel and had signed a contract with a private investigation company. The letter accused the program of using financial inducements to bring in players for football reasons. They said they were investigating whether residency and transfer information accurately reflected the students’ actual circumstances. The group even cited CIF Bylaw 510, which bans undue influence for athletic purposes in public schools. The Turnaround That Sparked Anger Westlake High School went from a winless season to a 10-1 record in Clausen’s first year. The team is now 7-3 and earned a spot in the playoffs after going 3-2 in their conference. He told the New York Post that he has inherited programs down on their luck before and turned them around. He said he will not apologize for doing what is needed to win. The coach believes that competition is a foreign concept for some families. He told reporters that some kids and families feel entitled to certain things. He said that mindset belongs to the old Westlake and does not align with the program’s direction going forward. Clausen added that everything in his program is earned through competition. He declared he would not apologize for constructing a program based on good families and good kids with college goals. Parents Feel Entitled To Playing Time Social media critics suggest the letter came from parents upset about their children not getting playing time. According to the letter, parents will file a formal request with the CIF Southern Section to investigate suspected recruiting violations. They claimed to have information that certain student-athletes had been approached about transferring for football reasons. No response was received after the school was contacted for comment. The letter was shared on X by Chris Fore, who noted the hits just keep coming at Westlake. I'm hearing that we are going to have big money vs big money in this case. Allegedly, a former NFLer whose son attends Westlake is being accused of financially incentivizing student-athletes to attend there. It will be interesting to see how this all shakes out. item.title: Shock anti-doping revelation: How Chris Lynn's positive cocaine test was kept under wraps
item.description: Shock anti-doping revelation: How Chris Lynn's positive cocaine test was kept under wraps originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australia's Chris Lynn served a one-month ban for cocaine use and completed a rehabilitation programme. His sample was taken on T20 Blast Finals Day, when Northamptonshire won the trophy. His ban was reduced to one month, and he reportedly joins Melbourne Renegades. Australian batter Chris Lynn tested positive for cocaine after T20 Blast triumph: Full report A positive cocaine test that stayed out of the public domain for weeks has now come to light, after England’s Cricket Regulator has revealed that Chris Lynn, the veteran Australian, served a one-month ban in August and has since gone through a rehabilitation programme. Lynn is 36, and his name has been a fixture of franchise cricket around the world for well over a decade. The trial began on 18 July, when Lynn went through a routine anti-doping check on T20 Blast Finals Day. He scored 39 and 4 that day as Northamptonshire won the trophy for the third time. His urine sample was then sent to a laboratory in France, where the analysis found benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine. That finding set the entire disciplinary process in motion. Case outcome: Chris Lynn ➡️https://t.co/wzk3vHLeEd https://t.co/k6nHPs3Vwe — Cricket Regulator (@CricRegulator) November 5, 2026 How the Chris Lynn anti-doping case unfolded after the T20 Blast final Lynn left for Sri Lanka almost straight after the Blast to play in the Lanka Premier League. He played only one game for Galle Gallants before being ruled out on 29 July with a leg injury. Two days later, the Cricket Regulator informed him of the adverse analytical findings in his sample and placed him under a provisional suspension. Roughly three weeks after that, Lynn publicly admitted that he had taken the drug. The statement he released explained when the use took place. He said it happened over a spell that stretched into the early hours of the following morning: “During a period of several hours across the evening of 15 July 2026 and into the early hours of 16 July 2026”. The timing adds a curious detail as earlier on that same evening of 15 July, Lynn had been forced to retire hurt in Northamptonshire’s quarter-final win over Gloucestershire, after a low full-toss from Duan Jansen struck him on the foot. Cricket Regulator ruling: Why Chris Lynn’s drug use was treated as out of competition The Regulator accepted Lynn’s explanation that he used the drug out of competition and that it had nothing to do with improving his sporting performance. That distinction matters a great deal under anti-doping rules, because it shapes how severe the sanction can be. Lynn was first charged under two articles of the ECB’s anti-doping rules. One of them was later withdrawn, since the amount of cocaine found in his sample fell below the minimum level that World Anti-Doping Agenc

item.title: Arch Manning and Texas get more bad news
item.description: Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on before the game between the Sooners and the Longhorns at Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns have won back-to-back games to get their season back on track, but they’ve been piling up injuries along the way. Texas already lost star left tackle Trevor Goosby for the season last month, and several other key players are banged up heading into Saturday’s road game against Missouri. Now, the Longhorns have been dealt another significant blow as running back Hollywood Smothers, who opened the season as Texas’ starter, will reportedly miss the rest of the year with a torn MCL, leaving an already struggling rushing attack even thinner. Texas’ Injury Woes Manning entered the season as a Heisman Trophy favorite, but back-to-back 27-24 losses to Oklahoma and Florida put him at risk of being benched. Head coach Steve Sarkisian even warned Manning that he would make a change if things didn’t improve. Texas responded with a 34-27 win over then-No. 7 Ole Miss on Oct. 24, but a key player went down during the game as Goosby was carted off in the first half with a knee injury and was later ruled out for the season , taking away the player responsible for protecting Manning’s blind side. Goosby, a preseason first-team All-American, is widely considered the top left tackle prospect in the upcoming NFL Draft. Texas was already shorthanded in that game, playing without pass rusher Colin Simmons and Smothers. Star wide receiver Cam Coleman also left the game with an injury. The Longhorns followed that up with a 31-3 win over Mississippi State last Saturday, as Manning threw three touchdown passes. But the offensive line issues were obvious, as Manning was sacked six times, and Coleman left early for the second consecutive game. “I think we still have better football out there that we have to go out and play,” Sarkisian said after the win, via the Associated Press . Smothers Out for Season On Thursday, Manning and the Longhorns got even more bad news this season, as On3’s Pete Nakos reported that Smothers will miss the remainder of the season. Smothers returned against Mississippi State after missing the games against Tennessee and Ole Miss with injuries, but he had just four carries for -6 yards before suffering another injury that will now rule him out for the remainder of the season. He has finished the year with 283 rushing yards and two touchdowns in six games. The NC State transfer had some big moments early in the season. In Texas’ 24-23 upset of then-No. 1 Ohio State, Smothers rushed for 74 yards and scored two touchdowns on the Longhorns’ final two drives to complete a fourth-quarter comeback. Smothers was one of the top running backs in the transfer portal after rushing for 939 yards and six touchdowns at NC State last season, earning first-team All-ACC honors. item.title: Franklin High football's MIAA playoff hopes dashed by Andover
item.description: The Franklin football team found itself in a spot it's in every year on Thursday night, November 5. The Panthers were back in the MIAA Division 1 state playoffs, a trip they have made each full season since 2019. Yet, for the fourth straight fall, the Panthers couldn't get over the first-round hump, as the eighth-seeded Panthers couldn't hold off hard-charging No. 9-seed Andover in a 56-21 victory for the visitors. It marked the third time since 2019 that Andover had defeated Franklin in the postseason. More: MetroWest high school football schedule/live scores (Nov. 5-7) Among the bright spots for the host Panthers (6-3) was sophomore quarterback Ethan Edmunds, who was 34-for-51 passing for 270 yards and three touchdowns in addition to 68 yards rushing. Additionally, Ben Scullin had eight catches for 65 yards and two TDs for Franklin, while Iyad Fraifer had nine catches for 102 yards and a TD. Christian Holmes added 13 catches for 86 yards for the Panthers. Andover will visit top-seeded St. John's Prep (9-0) in a quarterfinal clash (date, time TBA). item.title: Slick Jaguars breeze past rudderless Ravens 33-10
item.description: Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars threw for 242 yards and a touchdown pass (Patrick Smith) Trevor Lawrence guided the Jacksonville Jaguars to a straightforward 33-10 victory Thursday over a desperate Baltimore Ravens team forced to rely on its ailing third-string quarterback. Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown pass to Parker Washington, with Bhayshul Tuten running for a touchdown on the game's first drive and fellow Jaguars back Chris Rodriguez Jr. sealing victory on a dismal rainy night for Baltimore fans. Deprived of their talismanic quarterback Lamar Jackson and his backup Tyler Huntley due to injuries, Baltimore handed a first NFL start to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who played with enormous heavy strapping on his own injured ankle throughout. Fagnano battled gamely but there was little he could do to prevent the slick Jaguars from moving to 6-2. Having now won 14 of their last 16 regular-season games, Jacksonville's latest win further burnished their credentials as dark horses in the race for the NFL championship. "We've come together, I think we've got a great group that's all on the same page. We all think similarly. A bunch of hard workers," said Lawrence. "Everybody's gelling...You're seeing it come to life." The closing stages of a fourth straight loss for the Ravens -- who sank to 4-5 -- played out in front of emptying stands at the M&T Bank Stadium. Baltimore are already pinning their slim hopes of a playoff run on the expected arrival this weekend of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Lawrence began the night driving the Jaguars swiftly into the red zone with a 52-yard pass to rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher, before Tuten dashed across the line. The Ravens offense tried every trick in the book to protect their novice quarterback, with star running back Derrick Henry taking multiple direct snaps in wildcat formation. It yielded little, though Henry did move into 7th place in all-time NFL rushing yards, surpassing LaDainian Tomlinson. In the second quarter Lawrence sprang back to life with two superb passes, the first finding tight end Brenton Strange for a first down, before the second sent Washington 50 yards into the end zone. After a series of field goals, Rodriguez ran in a touchdown from a direct snap to make it 33-3. Baltimore's Justice Hill sprinted for a 65-yard touchdown to restore some pride with a late score. amz/sla

item.title: Ravens offensive line coach chucking tablet in pouring rain sums up dreadful TNF performance
item.description: Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images Ravens offensive line coach chucking tablet in pouring rain sums up dreadful TNF performance appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Emergency Baltimore Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano threw only 46 yards in three quarters. But the football wasn’t the only thing tossed in the rain during the Thursday letdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford showed his arm strength. By taking it out on a tablet during this viral moment. Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford is not happy 😳 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) (📺 PRIME) pic.twitter.com/KwgRWOSgDM — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 6, 2026 Ledford scolded his players for the offensive inefficiency. Fagnano not only struggled getting into a rhythm with the air attack. He took one sack as well as Jacksonville controlled the tempo throughout the night. Fagnano averaged a dismal 2.9 yards per play in the inclement weather. Jacksonville picked him off twice on the evening as well. But he wasn’t the only Raven who struggled against Jacksonville as he took over for both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley . Plus handled the QB duties on the same day Baltimore added Jacoby Brissett via the Arizona Cardinals. Star running back Derrick Henry couldn’t find much running lanes amid this offensive line play. Henry settled for 55 yards through three quarters but averaged just 3.4 yards per carry. Wide receiver Zay Flowers even handled some carries too, but hit 17 yards on three carries. Baltimore as a whole only hit 85 rushing yards entering the fourth quarter. The visiting Jaguars dominated across the line of scrimmage too, hitting three tackles for a loss. Baltimore matched the same output but again, the offensive line struggles rose as the story of this TNF showdown. Jacksonville turned to TNF to show it belongs in the conversation for one of the AFC’s best teams. They showed just that even if it meant Baltimore taking it out on a tablet. item.title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to Week 9 loss to Jaguars
item.description: Nov 5, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano (12) and Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) exit the field after the game at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens came into their Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars with low expectations – which they met. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano managed just 60 passing yards on a clearly-injured ankle, and the Ravens’ defense allowed far too many explosive plays through the air. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the 33-10 defeat: Zach Canter I don’t even know what to say or do at this point. We all knew this game had the potential to get ugly but I don’t think any of us had pictured exactly this ugly. I dont know where the Ravens go for here but there’s still eight more games to go. This product was unwatchable so as much as I hate investing more capital into the 2026 Ravens, the Jacoby Brissett trade seems necessary, just for the fact so the weapons on the outside don’t look as miserable as they did tonight. I don’t think I saw Zay Flowers smile once. At lot of questions need to be answered, but that won’t happen till this offseason. Until then, we trudge on and survive. Hopefully they’ll sell a few pieces at the deadline and kickstart the process. Kevin McNelis I’ve lived through some dark times as a fan of this team, but it’s been a while since I’ve felt this way. Maybe since the Super Bowl hangover when they lost a lot of pieces of the title team, but this iteration hints at some dark days to come with all of the bloated contracts and none of the payoff of having won a title. They should absolutely sell at the deadline. They need a hard reset on the roster and whatever it takes to shift the broken mentality of this group, especially that defense. My thoughts are with Jacoby Brissett. I just hope he goes out there and has some fun playing ball. Mark Myers Rock bottom. Everything that could have gone wrong did. The players plaguing the team with mistakes week after week kept doing so. The few standout players this year struggled today, adding insult to injury. The offense was putrid. Declan Doyle didn’t trust Joey Fagnano to push the ball at all, which is an even bigger statement on the state of a fully healthy offensive line. The defense continued to show a lack of effort. I wonder how Marlon Humphrey will blame the fans this time. Jacoby Brissett is definitely better than Fagnano, but not enough to make up for this woefully underperforming roster. Jacksonville is a great team, but they didn’t need to look like one to win convincingly tonight. Hopefully, the Ravens can show up for the occasion under the lights in Week 10 against the worst team in the league. But, man, I am struggling to find any reason to be excited for that game. Dustin Cox There really isn’t too much to say about this team right now. This simply isn’t a good enough

item.title: High Court Ruling: ADC heads to A’Court, insists Mark, Aregbesola remain party leaders
item.description: The 2027 presidential election campaign was thrown into fresh controversy, yesterday, as a Federal High Court in Abuja sacked the Senator David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, declared its emergence illegal and nullified all actions taken by the leadership, including the nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate. The judgment by Justice Peter Lifu, has triggered reactions, with the ADC vowing to challenge the decision at the Court of Appeal, Atiku alleging a calculated attempt by the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to cripple the opposition, and other political parties warning against actions capable of undermining democratic competition. While the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, SAN, hailed the ruling as justice well served, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, urged the judiciary to protect democracy and ensure certainty in the electoral process. The Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP, accused the APC of using the judiciary to foist a one-party state on Nigeria, while the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and other opposition figures expressed concern over what they described as attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the polls. The judgment came a day after Atiku held a campaign rally in Sokoto State, where thousands of supporters welcomed him as he began mobilising for the January 16, 2027, presidential election. Atiku, whose name had earlier been published by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, as the ADC presidential candidate, has already picked former Rivers State governor, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. The ruling, however, has cast uncertainty over the party’s leadership and presidential ticket, raising fresh questions about the legal and political battles that could shape the countdown to the general election. Court upholds Gombe’s suit Justice Lifu upheld the suit by Nafiu Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the ADC, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the party’s leadership. He consequently asked the court to nullify the actions of the Mark-led leadership and restrain Mark and Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary, respectively. The suit listed the ADC, INEC, Mark, Aregbesola and Nwosu as defendants. The plaintiff maintained that the emergence of the Mark-led leadership violated the party’s constitution and provisions of the Electoral Act. Justice Lifu upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought, declaring the Mark-led Caretaker Committee illegal and invalidating its actions. item.title: Jones - the smiling wind-up artist who refuses to fade away
item.description: Eddie Jones has coached in Australia, England, Japan and South Africa [Getty Images] An Eddie Jones press conference has always been an event in itself. You never quite know what's coming. A compliment, a cutting observation, a verbal grenade. Sometimes all three, invariably delivered with that mischievous smile. Jones belongs to a disappearing generation of coaches who understood that the contest could begin long before the players took the field. Warren Gatland could intimidate with his imposing presence and gruff demeanour alone. Jose Mourinho proclaimed himself 'The Special One' and made confrontation an art form. Jones was different. Small in stature, with an almost permanent grin, he could stir up an entire nation while thoroughly enjoying himself. All three built reputations on dominance. Not simply on the pitch, but over the agenda, their players and the organisations they represented. But the language of coaching is changing. Wales head coach Steve Tandy talks about connection and relationships. Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler emphasises collaboration, trust and understanding the person behind the player. Neither lacks ambition or authority, but their approach contrasts with the era of the all-powerful head coach. At 66, Jones remains one of rugby's most fascinating characters from that old school. The method behind the mischief In 2018 Jones questioned whether Wales fly-half Rhys Patchell could handle the pressure of playing England at Twickenham, while describing Warren Gatland's team as "confident and cocky". But his provocations sometimes crossed the line. That same year Jones apologised after footage emerged of him using some choice language to describe Wales and Ireland in less than flattering terms at a sponsors' event the previous year. The former was classic Jones. Identify a weakness, plant a seed of doubt and ensure everyone was talking about it. The latter showed when the wind-ups went too far. But how much was calculated? Speaking to BBC Sport prior to Japan's Nations Championship meeting with Wales, Jones offered an intriguing explanation. "Some of them were planned to an extent. Others might have come out of the press conference. Sometimes you say things at the press conference that you don't mean to say. But, yeah, sometimes." Players picked on form not club location - Tandy Jones looks to create Japan history in Cardiff Then came a surprising admission. "And particularly with England, I always felt with the English that they didn't have enough confidence in themselves." England? Lacking confidence? Jones explained that part of his responsibility was to provide that self-belief. "So I felt one of my roles was to give them that confidence, to be almost the battering ram for them." For Jones, the mind games served more than one purpose. Unsettling opponents was one thing, but taking pressure off his players was just as important. And if that meant making himself the centre of attention, so be it. The many sides of Eddie Jo

item.title: NBA rumors: Insider labels Raptors, Hornets as prime Domantas Sabonis trade destinations
item.description: Ed Szczepanski-USA TODAY Sports NBA rumors: Insider labels Raptors, Hornets as prime Domantas Sabonis trade destinations appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It’s no secret that the Sacramento Kings have been looking to trade away Domantas Sabonis to lean further into their ongoing rebuild. And with the Kings having started the season with just one win in eight games, trade talks involving the Lithuanian big man are only going to heat up the deeper we progress into the new campaign. To that end, ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel named the Toronto Raptors and Charlotte Hornets as prime trade destinations for Sabonis. “Two teams that looked to trade for him last year and had those trade conversations were the Toronto Raptors and the Charlotte Hornets,” Siegel said on the latest Clutch Scoops show. “The interest has not gone away. I can speak to that with certainty here. There’s been no new dialogue to report here but those are two teams that we’re keeping an eye on.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) (Fast forward to around the 33:30 mark.) Latest trade rumors/intel: Warriors, Thunder | Clutch Scoops with @TomerAzarly & @BrettSiegelNBA https://t.co/vjgWFuHgEd — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 5, 2026 Siegel then clarified why the Raptors or Hornets weren’t able to trade for Sabonis last season. The Kings did not want to take on Jakob Poeltl’s contract and could not find a third team to absorb the three years and $84 million left on his deal. Meanwhile, the Kings were demanding too much out of the Hornets (lottery picks during the 2026 NBA Draft) and Charlotte wasn’t budging. But at this point, perhaps the Raptors would be more inclined to trade for Sabonis. Poeltl has struggled immensely to begin the 2026-27 season, and Collin Murray-Boyles hasn’t yet solidified his place in the starting lineup. Toronto also has the defenders to help cover for Sabonis’ weaknesses on that end, and with the arrival of Kawhi Leonard, they are in win-now mode, which could nudge them towards a more aggressive approach on the trade market. Maybe the Hornets get desperate as well considering that their offense is currently the worst in the NBA. They need a new offensive hub following the departure of LaMelo Ball and amid the injury to Kon Knueppel, and if they keep losing, maybe they swing a trade for the Kings center. item.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick Does Damage Control Over Jets Drama
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Minkah Fitzpatrick cleared the air on Thursday, stating he actually said “Jets beating Jets,” not “Jets being Jets,” to explain the team’s self-inflicted errors. The veteran safety i nsists the comment never caused a stir inside the locker room, even as the 2-6 team fights to salvage their season. He believes the team knows exactly what he meant and that the media noise is just a distraction from the real goal: winning games. The New York Post reported that Fitzpatrick spoke on Thursday about the confusion following Sunday’s loss to the Raiders. He emphasized that the context of his words was clear to everyone in the room. “It hasn’t really caused any stir within this locker room,” Fitzpatrick said. “That’s the most important thing. Everyone in this locker room knew what I was talking about.” This focus on internal unity is crucial for a squad that has lost six of its last seven games. Distraction or Reality Check The controversy bothered Fitzpatrick more than anyone else because it threatened to take focus away from the field. He noted that talking about words he might have misused does not help a team trying to win. “It more so bothered me in the moment, when we’re a team that’s fighting to win, and we’re talking about stuff that doesn’t really matter,” he explained. The Jets are now set to face a Kansas City Chiefs team that has dropped two straight games after a hot start. Fitzpatrick is right to push past the noise. The team’s record shows a clear need for better execution, not more drama. He stated, “Our focus and objective now is to win and not focus on should’ve, would’ve, could’ve.” This mindset is the only path forward for a group that hasn’t won since beating the Browns on Oct. 11. The team needs to stop looking back and start looking at the next opponent. Injury Concerns Loom Large While the defense tries to stay focused, the offense faces its own hurdles. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson did not practice again on Thursday while remaining in concussion protocol. His absence would force the offense to rely heavily on other players like Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich admitted that Wilson is unique and hard to replace, yet the team remains confident in their depth. “In one respect, you can’t replace Garrett Wilson,” Reich said. “He’s a unique player. But on the other hand, we’re not afraid.” The team will adjust their game plan based on who is available on Sunday. David Bailey returned to full practice on Thursday after dealing with a groin injury, giving the line some stability. The Jets can only hope that things get better from here, because it can’t get much worse. The road ahead is steep for New York. They enter Sunday’s game in Kansas City looking to snap a losing streak, but that won’t happen unless they fix their penalties and miscues.

item.title: 'Leaders all over the world understand that Trump is only there for two more years & then he's gone'
item.description: In American politics, the possession of presidential power does not necessarily guarantee the capacity to exercise it. Few contemporary leaders have embodied this contradiction as dramatically as Donald Trump. Following what political scientist Ian Bremmer describes as the most consequential electoral reversal for a governing party in more than half a century, the founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media argues that the United States has entered a new political phase: the beginning of the end of Trump's capacity to dominate the domestic and international agenda. In this wide-ranging interview with France 24, Bremmer revisits his provocative thesis that America has already reached "peak Trump." Far from suggesting that the president has become powerless, he contends that his authority is increasingly constrained by congressional opposition, Republican discontent, unpopular foreign policy decisions and the growing awareness among international leaders that the present administration has a limited political horizon. The historical reversal is, in Bremmer's account, extraordinary: "Trump back in 2024 engineered for himself the biggest political comeback in American political history. And now, only two years later, the biggest loss in 50 years." At the heart of his analysis lies a fundamental distinction between institutional authority and political influence. Trump remains commander-in-chief, retains the instruments of executive government and continues to command extraordinary media attention. Yet Bremmer argues that the president's ability to translate those advantages into effective political outcomes is diminishing. The consequences, he suggests, extend far beyond Washington. From the war in Iran and the unresolved conflict in Ukraine to the future of transatlantic relations, America's allies and adversaries are beginning to adjust their strategic calculations to a post-Trump political landscape. As Bremmer puts it: "Those foreign leaders will start to engage more with the America that they expect to deal with after Trump is gone." Equally significant is his diagnosis of the domestic forces driving this transformation. Economic disillusionment, unfulfilled electoral promises and accusations of political self-interest have, in his assessment, undermined the very coalition that propelled Trump back to the White House. Meanwhile, the president's apparent preoccupation with monumental projects and personal legacy raises a deeper question about the relationship between political spectacle and the responsibilities of governance. Bremmer's conclusion is unambiguous: "Yes, two more years to go. But nowhere near the level of disruption that he had on the global stage at the beginning of this term." The interview ultimately raises a question of profound significance for American democracy and the international order: Can a president retain the formal powers of the world's most consequential political office while progressively losing the political authorit

item.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
item.description: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. Vendors of observability tools will be warming up their Indian sales teams today, because CERT-IN’s advice to Indian businesses includes improving their ability to log events, monitor for anomalies in real time, and send alerts. It also urged keeping test environments off the internet, and restricting access to cloud resources because CRAFTY FALCON is fond of using them to run its attacks. CERT-IN also warns that the attacks are “active and escalating” and therefore w

item.title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy. Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting. According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation. “The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said. Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow. “Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said. He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.” The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies. He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years. “For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. We must collectively work to bring an end to its rule. APC is the problem,” Ameh declared. The post Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh appeared first on Vanguard News .
